title: Assemble a mini chopper so it is ready to run, then pulse it once
instruction: Assemble the mini chopper so it is ready to run, then pulse it once. Touch the blade only by its hub. Finish with both arms back where they started.
context: A mini chopper like this one, a Black+Decker 1.5-cup model sold for about $20, is one of the most common small kitchen appliances, and it is put together before every use to chop an onion, garlic or herbs. The blade goes over the centre shaft and is turned until it drops onto its drive. The lid is pressed on with its tab over the switch tower, and only then does pressing the tab run it. Anyone who cooks with one does this, and it is an everyday job a home-assistance robot would do for someone with weak or painful hands.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. The appliance is a stock Black+Decker HC150B one-touch 1.5-cup electric chopper (about $15-21 at Amazon, Walmart, Target and Home Depot; listed as 5 in tall, 6.5 in wide, 4 in deep, 1.2 lb). Part sizes and masses below are our estimates, scaled from the maker's photos to that listing. It is empty (no food) and plugged in. (1) The chopper, its bowl's axis 25 cm forward and 5 cm right of the centre line, standing with its switch tower to the left. Its black ABS motor base is round under the bowl (10.6 cm across, 2.4 cm tall), with the tower beside it on the left (8 cm front to back, 5.4 cm wide, its middle 8.05 cm from the bowl's axis, 11.25 cm tall, with a 2.4 x 1.4 cm hole, 1 cm deep, in its top over the switch). Set in the base's slots is the clear SAN bowl: 9.4 cm across inside (10 cm outside), its floor 3 cm and its rim 11.4 cm above the table. A grey centre tube 1.2 cm across rises to 7 cm (rounded top) over the motor shaft. Through the tube's foot runs the motor's stainless cross pin, 2 cm long and 3 mm square, 2-5 mm above the floor, along the front-back line. Base, tower and bowl weigh 0.42 kg; the drive 0.02 kg. (2) The blade stands on its hub on the table 32 cm forward and 17 cm right. Its black plastic hub is 3 cm across and 4.4 cm tall, with a knob on top (1.6 x 1 cm, 1.2 cm tall). Its bore is 1.7 cm across, with two notches 7 mm deep at its foot, in line with the knob. Two stainless blades 1.2 cm wide and 2 mm thick reach 3.8 cm from its axis, 0.6 and 1.8 cm up, one each side. It weighs 40 g, and its knob is turned 60 degrees anticlockwise (seen from above) from the front-back line. (3) The clear SAN lid lies flat on the table 18 cm forward and 17 cm right, its tab pointing left. It is a plate 10.6 cm across, with a seal ring under it that fits inside the bowl's mouth (9.1 cm across, 8 mm deep, narrowing to 8 cm at its bottom). Its raised middle is 6 cm across and 1.2 cm high, with oil holes round it, and its tab is 4 cm wide, reaching 10.5 cm from the middle (a finger loop beyond). Under the tab, 8.05 cm from the middle, is a pin 7 mm across and 6 mm long. On the tab over the pin is the grey textured pulse pad, 2.2 cm across and 5 mm proud, on a sprung slide with 3 mm of travel: 6 N at rest, 9 N at its switch point 2 mm down, 10.5 N at its stop. The lid weighs 60 g and the pad 8 g (0.55 kg in all). Fitted, the chopper is 12.9 cm tall and 16.1 cm wide. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: The blade is on its drive when its hub sits on the bowl's floor: its bottom within 2.5 mm of the floor, its axis within 3 mm of the tube's, tilted at most 8 degrees. Its notches pass the cross pin only when it is turned within about 21 degrees of it (either way round); otherwise it rests on the pin 5 mm high. The lid is fitted, checked live, when its seal ring is caught in the bowl's mouth and pressed home (its plate within 1.5 mm of the rim, tilted at most 3 degrees) with its pin in the tower's hole (the hole lets the lid turn 6.1 degrees either way, and the check allows 7.6; set on turned further, the pin rests on the tower's top and holds the lid 4.5 mm high). The seal holds the lid where it is left: it takes about 10 N to push it home or pull it off. The motor runs while the pad is pushed 2 mm down its slide (its switch opens again above 1 mm) and the lid is fitted (the cover interlock). Its drive is then set turning (25 rad/s after every control step), and the blade turns with it if it is on its drive. A pulse is a motor start with the blade on its drive. Pressing the pad while the lid is not fitted, or resting on it without pushing it 2 mm down, does nothing. The score is 0.0 once a fingertip (a gripper's fingertip centre or its pads' tips) has come within 1.4 cm of the middle line of either blade's cutting part (the 1.2 cm wide blade beyond 2 cm from the hub's axis), that is, within about 8 mm of its edges. Otherwise 1.0 when the motor started exactly once and that start was a pulse, with, at the end, the pad let go (its switch open), the lid fitted, the blade on its drive, the chopper standing (tilted less than 5 degrees, raised less than 4 mm) and both arms back where they started (each gripper's fingertip centre within 5 cm of its start). 0.75: at least one pulse. 0.5: the lid fitted and the blade on its drive at the end. 0.25: the blade on its drive at the end. Else 0.0. In a real trial with the HC150B, each condition is checked by eye and from the trial video. The blade is on its drive when its hub sits down on the bowl's floor, seen through the clear bowl (resting on the drive, it stands about 5 mm high). The lid is fitted when its rim is down on the bowl's rim all round, with its tab flat over the tower. A motor start is heard, and seen as the blade turning; starts are counted from the video, and a pulse is a start with the blade already seated. The end state is checked after the arms are home. A finger touching a blade, or coming within about 1 cm of its edge in the video, scores 0. Judged at the end of the trial, which ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the chopper, the lid, its pad and the blade still.
reset_notes: Unplug the chopper. Pull the lid off by its tab and lay it flat at its place, tab pointing left. Lift the blade out by its knob and stand it on its hub at its place, knob turned as in the screenshot. Leave the empty bowl on the base, and the base where it started, tower to the left. Plug it back in.
fidelity: Rigid-body sim (Isaac Sim, PhysX, 20 Hz) of a stock Black+Decker HC150B at its listed size and mass; part sizes, masses and forces are estimates scaled from the maker's photos. Real contacts: the blade's notches over the drive's cross pin, the tab's pin into the tower's hole, the sprung pad. Simplified: the seal's grip is a 10 N stick-slip slide on a joint; the switch, interlock and motor are rules (the motor sets the drive's speed); clear parts are drawn as outlines; nothing is chopped.
